seoTitle: Window and Door Contractor Marketing Guide & Top Agencies
seoDescription: Learn what marketing works for window and door contractors, from local SEO to Google Ads, then compare top agencies and what to ask before you hire one.
content:
Window and door contractors get the most leads from local search: a complete Google Business Profile, a page for each product and service, strong reviews with project photos, and Google Ads on replacement keywords. Because most homeowners get more than one bid, fast follow-up matters as much as the lead.

Key Takeaways

Window and door buyers research carefully, compare several companies and often ask for more than one bid. Good marketing meets them at each step. Local SEO and your Google Business Profile get you found for searches like "window replacement near me." Separate pages for windows, entry doors, patio doors and repair help you rank for each job. Reviews and before-and-after photos build trust. Google Ads and Local Services Ads bring faster leads, while shared lead sites cost less to start but send the same lead to competitors. If you sell a major brand, ask about co-op marketing funds. Track every lead to a signed contract.

Why Window and Door Contractors Need Industry-Specific Marketing

Window and door jobs are big purchases, so homeowners research carefully and compare several companies before they sign. Many ask for more than one bid, and demand rises and falls with the seasons. Generic marketing misses these habits.

Good home service marketing fits the way these buyers shop. This post covers what works first, then compares agencies.

What Works in Window and Door Contractor Marketing

Seven things bring the most window and door leads. Here's how each one works.

Local SEO and Your Google Business Profile

Most homeowners start with a local search like "window replacement near me", so your Google Business Profile has to be complete. Pick a primary category that fits your main work and add secondary categories for the rest. Window installation and door supplier are common choices, but confirm the exact names inside your own account.

List every service you offer, add real project photos, and set your service areas. Keep your name, address and phone number the same on your website and every listing. Post weekly updates so the profile stays active. Our local SEO work follows this same checklist.

A Page for Each Window and Door Service

Give every main service its own page so you can rank for each one. Build separate pages for replacement windows, window repair, entry doors, patio and sliding doors, and storm doors. Cover window types such as double-hung, casement and bay as sections or their own pages.

Put the service and city in the title and H1. Each page needs photos, materials, a warranty note and a quote button. A good website design makes this easy to build and maintain.

SearchPageH1
replacement windows Denver/replacement-windows-denverReplacement Windows in Denver
entry door installation Austin/entry-doors-austinEntry Door Installation in Austin
sliding patio door repair Tampa/patio-door-repair-tampaSliding Patio Door Repair in Tampa

Google Ads and Local Services Ads

Google Ads bring leads faster than SEO while your rankings grow. Target replacement and installation keywords, and add negative keywords like DIY, parts and jobs so you don't pay for the wrong clicks. Use call tracking so you know which ads ring the phone.

Local Services Ads charge per lead and show a Google screening badge. Google checks license and insurance before it shows your business. Check Google's current rules to see whether your services qualify in your area. Our Google Ads management team sets up both kinds of campaigns.

Reviews and Before-and-After Photos

Homeowners trust what they can see, so show real jobs and real reviews. Ask for a review when the install is done, and reply to every review you get. Build a before-and-after gallery on your site and your Google profile. Get the homeowner's permission before you post photos of their home. Review management keeps this routine.

Fast Follow-Up and Lead Tracking

Most homeowners get more than one bid, so the first company to call back often wins. Respond to web leads within minutes during business hours. Track each lead's source through to a signed contract, and use a simple CRM to do it. Follow up on quotes that weren't signed. Good lead generation doesn't end when the form comes in.

Brand Dealer Co-op Marketing

If you're a dealer for a major window brand, ask the manufacturer about co-op marketing funds. Many manufacturers share ad costs with dealers, but rules vary by brand, so check your dealer agreement. Follow the brand's logo and claim rules. Highlight your local installation expertise next to the brand name.

Seasonal Campaigns

Window and door demand rises and falls with the weather, so plan campaigns ahead. Raise ad budgets before peaks. Use ENERGY STAR wording correctly when you make energy claims, and don't promise federal tax credits.

SeasonWhat to do
Spring and fallTypical install seasons. Raise ad budgets before they start.
WinterUse energy-bill and draft messaging.
SummerRun lighter ads and keep gathering reviews and photos.

How AI Is Changing Window and Door Marketing

AI tools now help window and door companies answer leads faster and show up in AI search answers. They don't replace the basics.

AI chat or texting can answer after-hours leads so they don't go to a competitor. AI can help draft service pages, but a person should edit every page. Appearing in ChatGPT and Google AI answers depends on clear service pages, consistent listings and reviews. No one can guarantee AI placement. Learn more about AI SEO.

Shared Leads vs Building Your Own Lead Flow

Lead sites can fill your calendar fast, but they often sell the same lead to several contractors. Compare shared and exclusive leads, and judge each source by cost per signed job, not cost per lead.

Owned channels like SEO, your Google profile and reviews keep working after you stop paying. Many contractors use both while their own lead flow grows.

Questions to Ask Before You Hire a Window and Door Marketing Agency

  1. Do you work with window, door or home improvement contractors now? Industry experience shortens the learning curve.
  2. Who owns my ad accounts, website and Google profile? You should own all three if you leave.
  3. Do you track leads to signed contracts? Leads only matter if they become jobs.
  4. How do you handle Local Services Ads? Setup and lead disputes take real work.
  5. How long is the contract? Long lock-ins limit your options.
  6. What are the fee and the ad spend? Ask for both numbers separately.

faqs.question: How do window and door contractors get more leads?
faqs.answer: Start with a complete Google Business Profile, a page for each service, and steady reviews with project photos. Add Google Ads for faster leads, and call new leads back quickly, because most homeowners compare several bids.

faqs.question: Is SEO or Google Ads better for a window and door company?
faqs.answer: Google Ads bring leads quickly but stop when you stop paying. SEO takes months to build but keeps bringing leads at a lower cost over time. Most contractors use both.

faqs.question: Are Local Services Ads worth it for window and door installers?
faqs.answer: They can be, because you pay per lead and appear above regular ads with a Google screening badge. Check that your services qualify in your area, and dispute leads that don't fit.

faqs.question: Should I buy leads from lead sites?
faqs.answer: Lead sites are fast, but they often sell the same lead to several contractors. Use them while you build your own lead flow from search, reviews and your website.

faqs.question: Can AI help market my window and door company?
faqs.answer: Yes. AI tools can answer after-hours leads and help draft content. Showing up in AI search answers depends on clear service pages, consistent listings and reviews, and no one can guarantee it.

faqs.question: How should window dealers use co-op marketing funds?
faqs.answer: Ask your manufacturer what ads and channels its co-op program covers, and follow its brand rules. Rules vary by brand, so check your dealer agreement before you spend.
